hook.en: On the night of 8 November 2016, most of the cash in people's wallets stopped being legal tender. Banks had long queues, and digital wallets suddenly became popular.

say.en: On the night of 8 November 2016, most of the cash in people's wallets stopped being legal tender. Banks had long queues, and digital wallets suddenly became popular. In this lesson: Explain the meaning of demonetisation.
State its features and aims.

body.en: On 8 November 2016, the Government of India announced that ₹500 and ₹1000 notes would no longer be legal tender. People could deposit or exchange the old notes in banks within a time limit. New ₹500 and ₹2000 notes were issued.

points.en: Old ₹500 and ₹1000 notes ceased to be legal tender
Old notes could be deposited in bank accounts

explanation.en: Demonetisation (8 November 2016) withdrew ₹500 and ₹1000 notes to tackle black money, fake notes and corruption, and to push savings and payments into formal, less-cash channels.

It is seen as a __3__ measure that brings unaccounted cash into the open. It also aimed to curb __4__ currency, to channel savings into the __5__ financial system and to move towards a __6__ economy.

say.en: Complete the summary of demonetisation.

body.en: *Demonetisation* is seen as a tax administration measure that brings unaccounted cash into the open. It was also a measure to curb corruption, counterfeit currency and terror financing, to channelise savings into the formal financial system, and to create a less-cash economy.

points.en: Curbing corruption, fake currency and terror funding
Channelising savings into the formal system

problem.en: After November 2016, a Davanagere cloth merchant who used to deal only in cash opened a current account, registered for UPI payments and began recording all his sales. Which features of demonetisation are seen?

steps.en: Moving from cash to UPI: towards a less-cash, digital economy.
Depositing cash and recording sales in a bank: channelising savings into the formal system.
Recorded sales can be assessed for tax: a tax administration measure.

answer.en: Less-cash economy, formal savings, and tax administration.
